questions.question: Distinguish between fixed and variable costs and give two examples of each for an Entrepreneur's Day stall.
questions.expected_answer: Fixed: stay the same regardless of how many units are sold, e.g. table hire, banner/posters, equipment hire, gas. Variable: change with each unit produced, e.g. ingredients, cups, bags, labels, serviettes.

questions.question: A team plans to make 60 bags of popcorn. Fixed costs R90; variable cost R3 per bag. Calculate total cost, cost price per bag, and profit if all sell at R8.
questions.expected_answer: Variable = 60 × R3 = R180. Total cost = R90 + R180 = R270. Cost price = R270 ÷ 60 = R4,50. Income = 60 × R8 = R480. Profit = R480 − R270 = R210.

questions.question: Using the popcorn figures above, calculate the break-even number of bags and explain what it means.
questions.expected_answer: Contribution per bag = R8 − R3 = R5. Break-even = R90 ÷ R5 = 18 bags. Selling 18 bags covers all fixed and variable costs of those bags; every bag sold after 18 adds R5 profit.
